source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.8.3 Operations on Graphs (PDF 114, printed 111). The DFS building example describes exploring each floor completely, which reads more like level-by-level search; the lesson keeps the hallway-to-the-end idea. Flagged. MCQ 9 is answered (b); the key gives (c). Recorded.

items: Insertion: add a vertex or edge, such as a new city and its roads.
Deletion: remove a vertex or edge; removing a city also removes all its roads.

Traversal: visit all vertices systematically with BFS (all immediate neighbours first, level by level, like taking every train from a central station before going further) or DFS (as far as possible along a branch before backtracking, like exploring one hallway to its end and then going back).
Searching: find a particular vertex or edge, such as a city or route.

blocks.prompt: Which traversal explores all immediate neighbours of a vertex before the next level (MCQ 9)?

items: Graph operations: insert, delete, traverse (BFS, DFS), search.
